dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: vastvantare vedyamāne sarvavastuṣu śūnyatā | tām eva manasā dhyātvā vidito 'pi praśāmyati ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: While one particular object is being perceived, there is emptiness with regard to all other things; meditating with the mind on that very emptiness, even though the object is still known, one becomes calm.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: contemplating that vacuity with a thought-free mind, only the light of consciousness remains; the differentiating mind comes to a standstill, so even while the perceived object is still present, the mind is dissolved in peace. He contrasts it with verse 120: there one withdraws from the perceived object itself; here one contemplates the emptiness of all other objects. Wallis: 'the emptiness of all things'.
dharana.technique_name: While One Thing Is Known, the Emptiness of All Others
dharana.instruction: While you perceive one thing, rest attention on the emptiness of everything else.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 97' = verse 122 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 122 = 'The emptiness of all things (Y97 ~ C2)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 122 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 122: The emptiness of all things (Y97 ~ C2)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 122 'Dharana 99', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 97. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 122 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: all other things, empty in that moment
the mind resting in that emptiness
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is a single object in focus with everything else in the field empty, and attention resting in the emptiness.
geometry.svg_hint: one small filled shape in a wide empty field
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Rest in the empty rest
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: while one thing is known, attention rests on the emptiness of everything else, and the mind calms. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The emptiness of everything other than the one thing being perceived
attention.secondary: Calm, even while that one thing is still perceived

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: While one particular object is being perceived, there is emptiness with regard to all other things; meditating with the mind on that very emptiness, even though the object is still known, one becomes calm.
adiyogi.method_summary: Look at, or listen to, one simple thing. Notice that, in this moment, everything else is absent: empty. Rest attention in that emptiness, letting the one thing remain known in the background.

honesty.disclosure: Door 097 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 97 (verse 122) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 097 is dharana 97, verse 122. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
New door researched on 2026-10-06 on branch research/vbt-houses-2-7; awaiting guardian review.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If attention strains, let it rest on the one object for a while. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit with one simple thing to look at or listen to. The map is one thing known, everything else empty.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Perceive one simple thing. Everything else, right now, is absent. Rest in that emptiness, the one thing still known.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: one shape in an empty field. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 122: while one object is perceived, all other things are empty; meditating on that emptiness, even while the object is known, one becomes calm.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Release the attention. Feel the weight of the body on its support. Open the eyes when ready.
